feature: Generic indirect-object rule and reference chains
source_location: ISO primary §7.3.10, printed pp. 33–34. On printed p. 34 it states the direct/indirect semantic equivalence rule; its preceding note permits reference chains.
ledger: 7.3.10 implemented; no new gap is inferred from an entry being direct or indirect without checking that entry's own requirement.
code: `pdf_syntax::Document::resolve` follows bounded chains; `get_key` looks up and resolves the entry. Raw `Dictionary::get` is used when reference identity or a source-mandated indirect reference matters.
assertions: Syntax-level chain handling is covered separately; this shard's drafts exercise public annotation/link consumers rather than duplicating the generic parser tests.
verdict: No generic direct/indirect equivalence defect identified.
residuals: Valid direct-only and indirect-only exceptions must remain entry-specific; `get_key` cannot replace raw access where the clause requires an indirect reference or the consumer needs object identity.

feature: Common annotation /Rect, /F, /AP, /AS and related values through the page annotation consumer
source_location: ISO primary §12.5.2 Table 166, printed pp. 467–468. Table identifies `/Rect` as a rectangle, `/F` as integer, `/AP` as appearance dictionary, `/AS` as name, without direct-only restrictions. `/P` is specifically an indirect reference to the associated page; preserve that exception.
ledger: The current ledger marks §12.5.2 departed for a writer-side `/AP` omission in specified text-layout cases; that departure is separate from the indirect-value reader question. Existing annotation render, AP-state, flags and blend tests mostly use direct scalar/array entries, while AP streams/subdictionary entries are indirect as required for streams. Table 166 `/CA` and `/ca` apply when the annotation appearance is regenerated and shall not be used if it has a stored appearance; the current `annotation::opacity` helper resolves indirect numbers on the construction path. Stored AP blend mode is source-required and reads through `get_key`; parent is already reviewing the stored `/BM` pixel test, so this shard avoids duplicating it.
code: `annotation::rectangle` and `annotation::numbers` resolve `/Rect` and every array member; flags and blend use `get_key`; appearance selection resolves `/AP`, `/N`, `/AS`, the state dictionary and its selected stream.
assertions: `annotations.rs`, `appearance_state_precedence_spec_audit.rs`, `stored_annotation_blend_spec_audit.rs`, and `widget_annotation_spec_audit.rs` exercise the consumers, but do not jointly establish indirect references for the Rect array and all Rect elements/flags/AP-state path.
verdict: Code path appears to honor valid indirect values. Draft one public pixel regression with direct controls to make that cross-cutting promise explicit; it is not a known defect.
residuals: Do not make `/P` direct in fixtures: source specifically requires it indirect. The annotation itself is indirect in the fixture to match page `/Annots` practice and avoid producer-validity ambiguity.

feature: Link destination/action values, common action `/S` and `/Next`, and destination-array operands
source_location: ISO primary Table 176 printed p. 482; action Table 196 printed p. 506; Table 202 printed p. 511. These define `/A` and `/Dest`, action type `/S`, `/Next` as action dictionary or array, and GoTo `/D`; no blanket directness requirement is added. Destination arrays can contain object references as well as direct numeric/name operands.
ledger: Link annotation and action rows are implemented with direct-destination, action-chain and public target evidence.
code: `link::links` passes raw `/A` to action `read`, whose walker resolves either direct dictionaries or references; `link::destination` passes raw `/Dest` to `Destination::read`, which resolves it. `Destination::View::read` resolves each array operand. Action `/S` is fetched with `get_key`; `/Next` is explicitly resolved and recursively walked.
assertions: Existing `links.rs` is corpus-level and direct-target-oriented; `actions.rs` covers performed chains. A paired exact-xref public target fixture would make the indirect action+destination array path independently reviewable.
verdict: No parsing defect found; optional draft provides one public integration assertion with direct expected-value control.
residuals: Some entries intentionally require references, e.g. Table 166 `/P`, Table 213 movie `/Annotation`, and GoToDp `/Dp`; current raw-reference reads preserve those constraints. Do not broaden support to malformed direct values in such slots.

feature: Reference-required action targets preserve identity instead of accepting a direct object
source_location: ISO primary Table 213 movie action describes `/Annotation` as an indirect reference; rendition action and GoToDp requirements specify indirect targets in their own tables/clauses. GoToDp is separately audited by the DPart shard.
ledger: Action type rows are implemented; no new incomplete directness exception identified here.
code: Movie target matches raw `dict.get("Annotation")` and only accepts `Object::Reference`; rendition's annotation and GoToDp target likewise preserve references. Generic direct action dictionaries and generic `/Next` are separately resolved.
assertions: Existing action tests cover action behavior and target identity; this shard does not duplicate the GoToDp control or broaden scope into its DPart semantics.
verdict: Entry-specific reference constraints are not evidence against §7.3.10; implementation distinguishes generic indirectability from entries whose schema requires a reference.
residuals: Action family review is sampled, not whole-clause certification.
